title: SIRCAFormer: Target-centred SAR change-guided reconstruction of Sentinel-2 reflectance across heterogeneous landscapes

affiliations.1: State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS), Wuhan University, Wuhan 430072, China
affiliations.2: Key Laboratory of Automatic Target Recognition, School of Electronic Science, National University of Defense Technology, 410073, China
affiliations.3: Institute of Space Earth Science, Nanjing University, Suzhou, China

abstract: Optical acquisition gaps leave target-date surface reflectance unobserved, while SAR changes provide complementary information whose optical interpretation varies across landscapes. We propose SIRCAFormer to reconstruct missing Sentinel-2 reflectance from bracketing optical images and three-phase SAR observations. A temporal CNN–Transformer backbone produces a base estimate, and a separate correction branch combines signed SAR changes on both sides of the target date with observed optical evolution. Local cross-attention associates these changes with reconstruction features, and bounded band-specific residuals refine the frozen backbone prediction. On an AOI-disjoint test set spanning six landscape categories, SIRCAFormer achieved the lowest pooled MAE and RMSE and the highest PSNR and SSIM among four representative comparison methods. Relative to Direct SAR Fusion using the same input observations, MAE and spectral angle decreased by 2.33% and 2.96%, respectively, with lower MAE in 13 of 17 test AOIs. Gains varied across landscapes and diminished under larger before–after optical changes. These results demonstrate that explicit target-centred SAR changes, interpreted with optical temporal context, can improve missing-date reflectance reconstruction beyond their use in the temporal backbone.
